doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Back at A&T and the Mombassa Club
summary: Discharged after eleven months, he finished coursework and began playing commercially at the Mombassa Club with Billy Tolles and Nipsey Russell as emcee.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: When were you discharged from the Navy?
I don’t know...it was the summer of ‘45.
So you were only in for a few months.
So you went back to Greensboro after that?
Yeah, I went back to A&T. A&T College.
At this point, were you starting to be a professional musician?

No, not at that point. When I went back, it was the middle of the semester, and I didn’t stay on the campus. I had to get me a room out in the town. I was still making up some courses that I had lost during those 11 months. After I got the courses made up, I started actually to play a little commercial music in a club called the Mombassa Club. The guy I told you about, Billy Tolles, he had the band. Nipsey Russell was the comedian. First job Nipsey ever played. Nipsey was a Lieutenant in the Army, and he was a very smart guy, as you know, if you watch him on TV. He came to Greensboro, and settled, and started working as an emcee in this club.
